title: Local tests retain the sunspot decline near 1981 but do not fix its date to the production transfer
abstract: We test whether the reported sunspot-number fall near January 1981 is an abrupt break at the Zurich-to-Brussels transfer. We use daily SILSO V2 sunspot numbers, adjusted F10.7 and measured Bremen Mg II data from 1978 to 2026. We fit local trends in monthly index relations, compare break dates, and test later active periods. On common observation days, separate local slopes with 24 months on each side give sunspot-number factors of 0.887 at matched F10.7 and 0.872 at matched Mg II. Conditional 95 percent intervals are 0.807-0.975 and 0.756-1.006. Matching observation days does not remove the fall. In fixed early-period fits, the best break dates occur in 1982, not January 1981. Later active-period tests often give changes of the same size. The relation changed, but these data do not identify the production transfer as its cause. The tests cannot separate solar structure from sunspot calibration. The study provides reproducible tests and model results; external index series remain outside the publication.
